newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: VA Tech takes market by surprise, H1 well up.
newsitem.headline: VA Tech takes market by surprise, H1 well up.

text.p: Austrian engineering group VA Technologie said on Wednesday group net profit soared 29 percent in the first six months but reiterated it expected the full year to be weighed down by an increased tax burden.

"For 1996 as a whole, the profit from ordinary activities, order intake, turnover....should again show substantial, continuous growth. The net profit will be burdened by higher taxes due to the postponed use of tax loss carry forwards," VA Tech said in a statement ahead of its earnings conference.

For the first half, VA Tech said pre-tax profit surged 50 percent to 484 million schillings ($45.5 million) , sales jumped 32 percent to 12.2 billion while net profit rose to 378 million from 294 million in the year-ago period.

VA Tech attributed the strong earnings to a surge in orders, with the order intake jumping 20 percent to 20.3 billion schillings. By division, plant engineering and services notched up the biggest rise with an increase of 48 percent.
The batch of earnings far exceeded analysts' expectations, which pegged pre-tax profit at around 370 million schillings and net profit at some 300 million schillings.

Traders cited stepped-up demand from investors following the strong earnings with VA Tech stock initially jumping 17.5 schillings to 1,348, before slipping back to stand 5.5 schillings higher in an overall limp Vienna market.
For the full year, VA Tech said it expected to post double-digit growth in all key earnings apart from in net profit and that it would pay out at least an unchanged dividend of 28 schillings.

"Growth will be higher than that from 1994 to 1995," chief executive Othmar Puehringer told journalists in reference to pre-tax profit. In 1995, pre-tax profit jumped 12.8 percent to 1.27 billion schillings.

Chief financial officer Helmuth Hamminger cautioned, however, that growth in the second half would be more moderate than the 50 percent surge posted in the first half of the year. -- Julia Ferguson, Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 254 ($ = 10.64 Austrian Schillings)
